assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: discountForTripCount, countSingleTicketsInWindow, discountForCategoryAndTripCount are three separate @TableTest methods

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented
assertions.evidence: "Child gets a flat discount regardless of trips | CHILD | {1, 5, 40} | 20"

assertions.text: Multiple tiers derived from 'every fifth trip' rule, boundaries, max 40% represented
assertions.evidence: "Exactly at the cap | 40 | 40" and "Beyond the cap stays capped | {41, 45, 100} | 40"

assertions.text: 30-day rolling window boundary tested: 30 included, 31 excluded
assertions.evidence: "Exactly 30 days ago is still in window ... 1" and "31 days ago has fallen out of the window ... 0"

assertions.text: 30-day window exercised at time-of-purchase granularity, not whole days only
assertions.evidence: All history entries use whole 'daysAgo' integers like 29/SINGLE, 30/SINGLE, 31/SINGLE; no hour-level distinction present

assertions.text: Value sets contain exactly the values that produce the same discount, no cross-tier contamination
assertions.evidence: "Below first tier | {1, 2, 3, 4} | 0" and "Within first tier | {6, 7, 8, 9} | 5" correctly grouped

assertions.text: Discount ladder table uses value sets for ticket count column to group counts within same tier
assertions.evidence: "Within seventh tier | {36, 37, 38, 39} | 35"

assertions.text: Tier-to-discount mapping expressed once, not repeated across multiple tables
assertions.evidence: discountForCategoryAndTripCount and calculatesDiscountEndToEnd both re-test specific tier mappings (e.g. 10→10%, 5→5%) alongside discountForTripCount

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 4 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: @Description present and provides context beyond rows
assertions.evidence: "The trip ladder: every 5th single ticket in the rolling 30-day window ... Trips In Window is the derived count fed in directly..."

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Eligibility/passenger-type table includes a Zone column with value set showing discount applies regardless of zone
assertions.evidence: discountForCategoryAndTripCount table columns are 'Traveler Category | Trips In Window | Discount?' with no Zone column

assertions.text: The rolling-window counting concern shows by row that a past purchase's zone does not affect whether it counts toward the travel count
assertions.evidence: "Zone does not affect the count | [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 2/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 3/SINGLE/ZONE_3] | 3"

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR} in at least one row
assertions.evidence: "Adult and senior are capped the same | {ADULT, SENIOR} | 45 | 40"

assertions.text: All 9 discount tiers are represented in the ladder table
assertions.evidence: Only tiers 0,5,10,35,40 appear explicitly; 15,20,25,30 tiers are missing from the discountForTripCount table.

assertions.text: Each tier is expressed as a single row with a value set for ticket counts, not split across multiple rows
assertions.evidence: "Exactly at first tier | 5 | 5" and "Within first tier | {6, 7, 8, 9} | 5" are two separate rows for the same tier.

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively
assertions.evidence: "[1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 15/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 29/SINGLE/ZONE_1]" encodes days-ago values rather than absolute dates.

assertions.text: Multiple tables address distinct concerns, not one monolithic table
assertions.evidence: Separate methods: discountForTripCount, countSingleTicketsInWindow, discountForCategoryAndTripCount, calculatesDiscountEndToEnd.

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules
assertions.evidence: Each @TableTest table (e.g. countSingleTicketsInWindow with 7 rows) targets a single concern without combining unrelated dimensions.

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable
assertions.evidence: Expectation values vary across rows, e.g. "Below first tier | {1,2,3,4} | 0" vs "Exactly at first tier | 5 | 5", not a fixed value.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body
assertions.evidence: Description states "every 5th single ticket ... raises the discount by 5%, up to a 40% cap", and 30-day boundary rule is described in the counting table's @Description.

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or fallback method name) states what the code under test does
assertions.evidence: Method names like "discountForTripCount" and "countSingleTicketsInWindow" describe the computation performed, not an external regulation.

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on, and which the table holds constant for every row, must be visible as a column or named in the @DisplayName/@Description as deliberately held fixed.
assertions.evidence: PURCHASE_TIME field only used to construct relative days-ago timestamps; outcome depends on relative offset (encoded in History column via daysAgo), not the absolute PURCHASE_TIME value, so it is a fixture value the rule is indifferent to.

assertions.text: When a title or description quantifies over a domain, the rows must actually cover that domain.
assertions.evidence: "Zone must never affect the count." is backed by rows using ZONE_1, ZONE_2, ZONE_3; "CHILD ... independent of travel frequency" is backed by "Child gets a flat discount regardless of trips | CHILD | {1, 5, 40} | 20".
